This 
 document outlines the equipment inspection checklist I1, which must be performed 
 every six months as indicated by M6 in the title block

The IMO 
 Pump operate equally efficiently with both Light and Heavy oils and with 
 Liquids having similar Lubricating properties. Its purpose is to Pump oil to 
 fuel nozzle.

Must be 
 greased through one nipple every 4000 operating hours on oil firing

Bearing 
 must be replaced every 3 years of operation on oil firing.

Axial type mechanical seals are intended to prevent the 
 leakage of fluid along the driven shaft of a pump. In order to insure that the 
 seal does not wear during operation, it must be lubricated by pumped liquid. 
 An insignificant amount of leakage may therefore occur and suitable provision 
 should be made for collecting this leakage. If there is excessive fuel leakage 
 the mechanical seals must be replaced as the following:

items:
Remove the screws (130 A) of the ball bearing, undo the front 
 cover (501) and the screws (451). Be careful with the O- ring gasket (506). 
 Remove the washer (130) and back off the power rotor carefully out of the pump 
 stand the power rotor with the sealing washer (139) resting on two wooden 
 crossbars. See fig. 1a.

Undo the locking washer (123) and back off the bearing nut 
 (124). Tap the shaft end lightly with the tin mallet until the ball bearing 
 (122) releases the power rotor the inner ball ring is then supported by the 
 distance sleeve (120). See fig. 1.

Lift the ball bearing (122). Releases retaining cover (527), 
 guiding bush (5110) and mechanical seal (509) from the power rotor. Remove the 
 distance sleeve and the sealing washer with the O- ring gasket (139/140) is 
 released.

Press the sealing bush( 509A- D) out of the guiding bush 
 (5110).when necessary the O- Ring gasket (511 A) can be released.

The ball bearing is always to be washed 
 in the new white spirit. Take Great Care to protect the ball bearing when pump 
 parts are being washed as used Solvent is not clean and can therefore soil the 
 race.

items: This takes place in reverse order

Place the O- Ring (140) in its groove in the power rotor. Ease 
 the sealing washer (139) over the O- Ring. Pass the sleeve (120) onto the 
 shaft end and smear the upper side of the sealing washer (139) with grease.

Reassembly see fig- the spring unit (506B) in its groove and 
 bush the seal (509) into the guiding bush (5110) being mindful of the O- Ring 
 (509B) and make sure also that the sealing bush (509A) engages with the 
 locating pin (502).

Pass the guiding bush with seal (5110)/509) on the power 
 rotor. Fit the grease retaining cover (527) and bush the ball bearing into the 
 shaft.

Apply the bearing locater to the inner ring of the ball 
 bearing onto the shaft and fit the mounting screw into the centre hole on the 
 shaft end. See fig. 1b.

Advance the nut and washer of the mounting screw in order to 
 push the inner ring of the ball bearing into its proper position on the shaft 
 end and check that the sealing bush (509A) engages with the locating pin 
 (502). Secure the ball bearing on power rotor with the bearing nut (124) and 
 locating washer (123)
 CAUTION Never strike the ball holder or 
 outer ring of the bearing.

Mount the power rotor in the pump. Place the washer (130) on 
 the outer ring of the bearing .mount the front cover (501) to the pump casing. 
 Fasten the outer ring of the bearing with the screws (130A) prepare pump of 
 the testing. Proceed in accordance with the instructions given under the 
 heading (Starting up).

Inspection of 
mechanical seal
Axial type mechanical seals are intended to prevent the 
 leakage of fluid along the driven shaft of a pump. In order to insure that the 
 seal does not wear during operation, it must be lubricated by pumped liquid. 
 An insignificant amount of leakage may therefore occur and suitable provision 
 should be made for collecting this leakage. If there is excessive fuel leakage 
 the mechanical seals must be replaced as the following:
Dismantling of Mechanical Seal
Remove the screws (130 A) of the ball bearing, undo the front 
 cover (501) and the screws (451). Be careful with the O- ring gasket (506). 
 Remove the washer (130) and back off the power rotor carefully out of the pump 
 stand the power rotor with the sealing washer (139) resting on two wooden 
 crossbars. See fig. 1a.
Undo the locking washer (123) and back off the bearing nut 
 (124). Tap the shaft end lightly with the tin mallet until the ball bearing 
 (122) releases the power rotor the inner ball ring is then supported by the 
 distance sleeve (120). See fig. 1.
Lift the ball bearing (122). Releases retaining cover (527), 
 guiding bush (5110) and mechanical seal (509) from the power rotor. Remove the 
 distance sleeve and the sealing washer with the O- ring gasket (139/140) is 
 released.
Press the sealing bush( 509A- D) out of the guiding bush 
 (5110).when necessary the O- Ring gasket (511 A) can be released.
** CAUTION
The ball bearing is always to be washed 
 in the new white spirit. Take Great Care to protect the ball bearing when pump 
 parts are being washed as used Solvent is not clean and can therefore soil the 
 race.
Reassembly of Mechanical Seal
This takes place in reverse order
Place the O- Ring (140) in its groove in the power rotor. Ease 
 the sealing washer (139) over the O- Ring. Pass the sleeve (120) onto the 
 shaft end and smear the upper side of the sealing washer (139) with grease.
Reassembly see fig- the spring unit (506B) in its groove and 
 bush the seal (509) into the guiding bush (5110) being mindful of the O- Ring 
 (509B) and make sure also that the sealing bush (509A) engages with the 
 locating pin (502).
Pass the guiding bush with seal (5110)/509) on the power 
 rotor. Fit the grease retaining cover (527) and bush the ball bearing into the 
 shaft.
Apply the bearing locater to the inner ring of the ball 
 bearing onto the shaft and fit the mounting screw into the centre hole on the 
 shaft end. See fig. 1b.
Advance the nut and washer of the mounting screw in order to 
 push the inner ring of the ball bearing into its proper position on the shaft 
 end and check that the sealing bush (509A) engages with the locating pin 
 (502). Secure the ball bearing on power rotor with the bearing nut (124) and 
 locating washer (123)
 CAUTION Never strike the ball holder or 
 outer ring of the bearing.
Mount the power rotor in the pump. Place the washer (130) on 
 the outer ring of the bearing .mount the front cover (501) to the pump casing. 
 Fasten the outer ring of the bearing with the screws (130A) prepare pump of 
 the testing. Proceed in accordance with the instructions given under the 
 heading (Starting up).
